title: Gunman who killed at least 6 in Kraków mass shooting has died in hospital | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

A gunman who killed at least six people during a deadly rampage in the Polishcity of Kraków on Saturday has died in hospital, police said on Monday.

The country was horrified by therare mass shootingin the historic main square of the city in the country’s south, which prompted two days of national mourning. Authorities said the attack was likely driven by far-right ideology.

The 24-year-old Polish suspect, named as Michał Oksiński, was shot and injured by police during the attack before being taken to hospital,according toPolish public broadcasterTVP.There, he underwent multiple surgeries and had been in a critical condition.

The mass shooting – which authorities are investigating as a possible terror attack – has generated shock and fear in a European nation with exceptionally tight gun laws.

Kraków police said the gunman drove into the city’s main market square, popular with both tourists and locals, and started firing randomlyfrom his car, killing four women and two men. Sixteen others were injured, including two police officers.

The alleged attacker was wearing military-style clothing and used “military weapons,” Police Deputy Inspector Katarzyna Cisło told Polish news outlet TVN24. Moreweapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle. However, he had no affiliation with the Polish military, according to TVP.

The bodies of his sister, mother and fatherwere later found at the suspect’s home in the town of Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 120 miles northeast of Kraków. Poland’s prosecutor’s office said Sunday that it is “highly likely” the killings were carried out by the same person, but investigations were ongoing.

Eleven firearms were recovered from both sites, the prosecutor’s office spokesperson said.

Little is known about the gunman and his motive was not immediately clear. But Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said that the shooter was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held “very radical views.”

Emblems on his clothing were being examined by experts, an interior ministry spokesperson said on Monday.

The man had a firearms license since March and attended a shooting club with his father, the state broadcaster reported,adding he was not known to police before Saturday’s shooting.

The attackerfired at least several dozen shots during the lethal rampage, according to a spokesperson for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, Przemysław Nowak.

Poland, like other European Union countries, has strict rules about acquiring guns and very few people are allowed to own military-style weapons or carry guns in public. About 411,000 people have gun permits in the country, which has a population of more than 37 million,according tothe Associated Press.

An off-duty surgeon who rushed to the scene of the shooting to treat victims of the attack, including a police officer, said he had just finished eating lunch with his family when he heard “what sounded like gunshots.”

Michal Pedziwiatr described being “in the eye of the storm” as he and a friend – also a surgeon – began providing care to the wounded.

Pedziwiatr told a press conference on Sunday that his friend, Mateusz Wierdak, was a “hero” for saving the life of a police officer who subdued the attacker, after he “applied pressure to the bleeding wound without any protective gear or gloves” and “stuffed gauze pads into the chest cavity,” Reuters reported.

The two wounded police officers, who Polish Prime ​Minister ‌Donald Tusk praised for also saving “many lives,” underwent surgery and remain in hospital, police said.

This is a developing story and will be updated.

CNN’s Charlotte Reck, Christina Zdanowicz, Billy Stockwell and Sana Noor Haq contributed reporting.

CNN’s Charlotte Reck, Christina Zdanowicz, Billy Stockwell and Sana Noor Haq contributed reporting.
